name: Helix Foundry Ontology and Knowledge Graph from Your Data
idSeed: Helix Foundry 0.1 Ontology and Knowledge Graph from Your Data
description: Connect databases and documents; an AI agent maps them into one graph.

upstream.version: commit c900024caa1c65157604d7ee84b1f60d7fbfc00d (2026-11-06, main); its local/compose.yaml runs foundry 0.1.2, foundry-site 0.1.3, ontology-agent 0.1.1, HelixDB v0.0.14 (foundry and site images built from c7de40515f56, which differs from the pin only in compose/README/test files)

FOUNDRY_GATEWAY_IMAGE.description: Caddy image this service's Docker build starts FROM (Railway passes it as a build argument).

PORT.description: Port the gateway listens on (public domain target and healthcheck).

BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME.description: User name for the browser's sign-in prompt. Letters, digits and . _ @ - (anything else falls back to admin).

BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD.description: Password for the browser's sign-in prompt, generated at deploy. Foundry has no sign-in of its own, so this protects the whole install; at least 12 characters or the gateway refuses to start.

FOUNDRY_AGENT_ENDPOINTS.description: on: /mcp and /v1/ontologies/... go straight to Foundry, which requires FOUNDRY_LOCAL_TOKEN as a bearer token (for Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP clients). off: they stay behind the password like the rest.

FOUNDRY_SITE_UPSTREAM.description: Foundry web app on the private network.

FOUNDRY_API_UPSTREAM.description: Foundry API (MCP and HTTP Ask) on the private network.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL on redeploy.

FOUNDRY_SITE_IMAGE.description: Foundry web app image this service's Docker build starts FROM (HelixDB's release image, unchanged). Upgrade it together with FOUNDRY_IMAGE and FOUNDRY_AGENT_IMAGE on Foundry.

PORT.description: Port the web app listens on (healthcheck).

HOSTNAME.description: Bind address of the Next.js server (:: = IPv4 and IPv6 on the private network).

HELIX_WFE_ORIGIN.description: Foundry API on the private network; the web app's /papi forwards to it with the owner token.

FOUNDRY_ORIGIN.description: The origin the web app believes it is served at. Keep it: the local build accepts only loopback origins, and the Gateway presents every request as localhost:3000.

FOUNDRY_LOCAL_TOKEN.description: Owner token the web app sends to Foundry (set on Foundry).

FOUNDRY_SAMPLE_DB_HOST.description: Host that Use the sample connects to (the Acme DB service), written into the web app at start in place of upstream's acme-db.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL on redeploy.

FOUNDRY_IMAGE.description: Foundry backend image the foundry binary and its config are copied from at build (HelixDB's release, unchanged).

FOUNDRY_AGENT_IMAGE.description: Ontology agent image this service's Docker build starts FROM (HelixDB's release, unchanged).

PORT.description: Port of Foundry's health listener, which Railway health-checks (/readyz). The API listens on 8081 (private).

FOUNDRY_LOCAL_TOKEN.description: Owner token, generated at deploy: the web app sends it to Foundry, and MCP clients send it as Authorization: Bearer. Whoever has it controls this install; at least 32 characters.

FOUNDRY_CONNECTOR_KEY.description: Key that seals every database password and API key given to Foundry, generated at deploy. Never change it: credentials sealed with it become unreadable. Back it up with your data.

FOUNDRY_S3_SECRET.description: Secret of the store's foundry identity (set on Storage).

HELIX_DB_DSN.description: Foundry's MySQL database (Go DSN). Foundry migrates it at every start.

HELIX_LOCAL__SITE_ORIGIN.description: Public URL of Foundry (the Gateway): links given to agents start here, and MCP and HTTP Ask answer only for this host. Change it when you add a custom domain.

HELIX_LOCAL__HELIX_URL.description: HelixDB on the private network: every ontology's loads share it.

HELIX_LOCAL__S3__ENDPOINT.description: The S3 store's public URL. Browsers upload documents to URLs Foundry signs for it, so Foundry uses the same public address.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.description: Optional. A Claude API key: Foundry then drafts, reads documents and answers with Claude. Leave empty to choose a provider and enter its key in Settings > AI models instead (stored sealed).

OPENAI_API_KEY.description: Optional. An OpenAI API key, used when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is empty. Leave empty to choose in Settings > AI models.

FOUNDRY_WORK_MAX_GB.description: GiB of snapshots one draft or one load may unpack into the /work volume (upstream: 6). Keep two of them below the volume size.

FOUNDRY_STARTUP_WAIT_SECONDS.description: Seconds the start waits for MySQL and the store before starting Foundry anyway (keep it below the healthcheck timeout).

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL on redeploy: a load or question in flight finishes or is handed back (the agent drains for 100 s).

HELIX_HTTP_ADDR.description: HelixDB's HTTP listener (IPv4 and IPv6 on the private network). It checks no key: never add a public domain or TCP proxy.

HELIX_DATA_DIR.description: Where HelixDB keeps its database (the volume).

HELIX_TELEMETRY_LEVEL.description: No telemetry, as upstream's compose file runs it.

RAILWAY_RUN_UID.description: Run as root so HelixDB can write the root-owned Railway volume (the image's user is 65532 and has no shell to change it).

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Time HelixDB gets to drain and close its storage on redeploy.

FOUNDRY_STORAGE_IMAGE.description: SeaweedFS image this service's Docker build starts FROM (the version upstream's compose file pins).

PORT.description: Port of the S3 API (public domain target and healthcheck).

FOUNDRY_S3_SECRET.description: Secret of the store's one S3 identity, foundry, generated at deploy. Foundry references it.

STORAGE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.description: Comma-separated origins whose pages may upload (CORS). Add your custom domain here if you give the Gateway one.

STORAGE_VOLUME_SIZE_MB.description: Size of each SeaweedFS volume file. Small files fit a 5 GB Railway volume; raise it on large volumes.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Time SeaweedFS gets to stop cleanly on redeploy (it takes about 20 s).

MYSQLUSER.description: MySQL user, used for the Data panel.

MYSQLDATABASE.description: Default database, used for Data panel.

MYSQLPASSWORD.description: Root password, used for Data panel.

MYSQL_DATABASE.description: Database to be created on image startup (Foundry's tables).

MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD.description: Root password for MySQL DB, generated at deploy (letters only: it sits in Foundry's DSN unescaped).

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Time MySQL gets to shut down cleanly on redeploy.

ACME_DB_IMAGE.description: Railway Postgres image this service's Docker build starts FROM.

PGDATA.description: Location where the database will be initialized.

PGHOST.description: Railway Private Domain Name (the Site writes it into Use the sample).

PGPORT.description: Port to connect to Postgres (the sample expects 5432).

PGDATABASE.description: Required variable for the data panel.

POSTGRES_DB.description: Database holding Acme Corp's sample tables. Keep acme: Foundry's Use the sample connects to it by that name.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.description: Superuser password, generated at deploy. Foundry uses the read-only login acme_reader instead (password acme, built into the web app; made-up data, private network only).

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Allow Postgres to cleanly shut down.
